domain: Travel & Expense (app code TE) — /app/travel-expense, 9 tabs + 13 settings panes. Entire surface is client-only React state persisted to a single browser localStorage key `apragya.workspace` (src/lib/workspace.tsx:68, read() :912, update() :940). There is NO server route for this app: src/app/api/v1 contains only auth, crm/leads, members, tenants. Nothing in the domain reaches a database, a mail system, a card provider, a bank file, or a ledger. Existing SQL conventions to follow live in migrations/0001_identity_and_tenancy.sql (uuid PKs, timestamptz, numeric(18,4) + char(3) currency, tenant_id on every business table, archived_at instead of DELETE, version column for optimistic concurrency); migrations/0004_platform.sql already provides app_settings / app_settings_changes (tenant_id, company_id, app_code, section, jsonb value, version, before/after) which is where TeSettings belongs.

entities.name: ExpenseReport
entities.purpose: A trip's worth of expenses submitted and reimbursed once. Today it is a title + a single flat total; there is no line-item table, no receipt, no claimant and no approver. Created by ExpenseReportsPane, advanced one status per click, and flipped to Reimbursed either by that button or by disbursing a run.

fields.notes: crypto.randomUUID() minted in the browser (workspace.tsx:1424). Server must mint its own.

fields.name: title
fields.notes: Free text. Dialog requires non-empty via disabled={!title.trim()} (panes.tsx:279) but the value is .trim()'d with no length cap and no uniqueness. Also abused as the category seed on the Dashboard (see notes on category).

fields.name: currency
fields.notes: Free-choice from 6 hardcoded currencies (travelExpenseData.ts:17-24). No FX rate, no base-currency amount, yet every total in the app is summed across currencies. Needs a companion base_amount numeric(18,4) + fx_rate numeric(18,8) + fx_rate_at timestamptz.

fields.name: status
fields.sqlType: text not null default 'Draft' check (status in ('draft','submitted','approved','rejected','reimbursed','cancelled'))
fields.notes: Prototype has no Rejected and no Cancelled state — a submitted report can only move forward (workspace.tsx:1441-1452). Production needs at minimum rejected + cancelled, plus a returned-for-edit state, or approvers have no way to say no.

fields.name: total
fields.notes: JS float today. Set once at create: 0 for a 'report', Number(amount)||0 for a 'quick' expense (panes.tsx:164). Never recomputed, never editable — a full report is permanently 0.00. Must become a derived/maintained sum of expense_items.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.notes: Client clock (workspace.tsx:1424). Also used as the Reports-tab date filter key and as the start of 'avg turnaround'.

fields.name: reimbursedAt

openQuestions: Per-diem rules: the app stores a single flat 'Default per-diem' string with no currency and lists both 'per diem' and 'per km' as policy limit categories. Real per-diem needs destination bands, domestic vs international rates, partial-day and meal-provided deductions, and effective-dated rate versions. NONE of this is inferable from the code — the rates, the bands and any statutory basis must come from the product owner. Do not invent them.
Mileage / 'per km' reimbursement rate: a limit category exists with no rate, no vehicle class and no effective date. Rates are frequently set by statute or tax authority and must not be invented.

Tax treatment: no expense record carries a tax amount, tax code, reclaimable flag or supplier tax id, and agency invoices (absent) would need them. Whether input tax is tracked or reclaimed on employee expenses, and under which jurisdiction, is unknown and must not be assumed.

Currency conversion: six currencies are selectable and every total sums them unconverted while the Reports tab claims 'tenant billing currency'. Which currency is the base, where FX rates come from, and whether the rate is locked at expense date / submission / approval / payment must be specified before base_amount columns can be defined.

Reimbursement payment rail: 'Batch Generation' is described as 'the bank file for disbursement' with no format, no bank account, no payee bank details and no export. The concrete file format and banking integration must be specified; do not assume NACHA, SEPA, BACS or NEFT.

Payroll coupling: many T&E products reimburse through payroll rather than a bank batch. Nothing in the code indicates which, and the repo has a separate Payroll app (code PAY). Whether reimbursements settle via payroll, via a bank file, or both, is unknown.

Corporate card feed: the importer accepts .csv/.ofx/.qfx by attribute but only parses commas. Which card provider(s), which feed format, whether it is a file drop or an API, and what unique transaction identifier the provider supplies (needed to replace the fragile date|merchant|amount dedupe key) are all unspecified. Do not invent a provider contract.

Receipt email-in: no mail provider, no inbound webhook, no address allocation scheme and no verification exist. Which provider handles inbound mail, how the tenant address is generated and verified, and what happens to mail from an unrecognised sender (reject, quarantine, create unattributed) must be decided.

OCR: agentCatalog ships a 'Receipt OCR Extractor' for this app with no implementation. Which OCR/extraction service, what confidence threshold auto-fills versus asks, and whether the raw response is retained (and for how long) are unspecified.

Approver resolution: approval levels are free-text labels such as 'Reporting manager' and 'Finance'. Whether an approver resolves from an HR reporting line, a role, a named user, a cost-centre owner, or a project manager is undefined — and there is no employees/HR table in migrations yet. Delegation and out-of-office reassignment are likewise unaddressed.

Approval semantics: does a threshold-bearing level replace lower levels or add to them? Must every matching level approve, or is any one sufficient? Does an amount change after partial approval reset the chain? The UI text ('climb these levels in order') is not precise enough to encode.

Self-approval and segregation of duties: today one person clicks Submit, Approve and Mark reimbursed. Whether a claimant may ever approve their own report, and what the minimum separation is between approver and disburser, is a policy decision.

Expense category taxonomy: three non-overlapping lists exist in code (12 lowercase policyCategories, 8 Title-Case expenseCategories, and the GL map keyed by the latter). Which is canonical, whether categories are tenant-editable, and whether they are hierarchical must be decided before expense_categories can be modelled.

Chart of accounts: GL account codes are free text with no validation. Whether a chart of accounts lives in this product, is synced from an ERP, or is per-company, determines whether gl_accounts is a table here or an external reference.

Project and budget-head sources: both travel-request fields are FK-shaped but empty (one option, one disabled control), and no projects or budget_heads table exists. Whether these come from the Project Management app, a finance module, or a new table is unresolved.
SLA semantics: 21 days from approval to disbursement — calendar days or business days? Which tenant calendar and holidays apply? What happens on breach (escalate to whom, notify, or report only)?

Multi-entity scope: migrations model companies within a tenant. Whether expense reports, policies, approval levels, GL mappings and SLAs are tenant-wide or per-company (app_settings already supports both via a nullable company_id) needs deciding per section.

Retention and personal data: receipts and card statements carry personal financial data. Retention periods, deletion on employee offboarding, and whether receipt images are exportable to the employee are unspecified — and the repo has a Compliance Center app whose retentionPolicies are not connected to T&E.

Travel-request lifecycle: 'Active' and 'Closed' are the only states. What the intended lifecycle is (draft → submitted → approved → booked → travelled → settled → closed, with cancellation), and whether a request can be edited after approval, has to be defined before the status check constraint can be written.

Agency invoice flow: the partner portal declares 'Travel invoices' but the review tab has no entity. What an agency may submit, whether it must reference a trip or segments, what accept/reject does downstream (payable? credit note?), and who is authorised to review are all unknown.

Duplicate-report policy: card auto-match currently permits many charges to match one report and a report to sit in two reimbursement runs. Whether a report may be partially paid, re-paid after a failed disbursement, or split across runs determines whether run membership needs per-report amounts and a payment-status column.
